claims.text: Classical EAM reference potentials inadequately cover the atomic configurations sampled by ab initio high-temperature multicomponent HEA liquids.
Replacing EAM references with an ML interatomic potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve coverage of relevant HEA configurations.
An ML potential can be trained on DFT configurations to describe both liquid and solid high-entropy material phases.
The proposed ML potential captures many-body interactions in complex HEA liquids and partially disordered solids.
Short-range ordering is characteristic of complex HEA liquids and partially disordered solids.
The proposed ML potential captures the short-range ordering of complex HEA liquids and partially disordered solids.
Training directly on high-temperature ab initio liquid data makes the ML reference sample the same configuration space as the target ab initio ensemble.
Improved reference–target configuration-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The ML reference will produce significantly lower systematic free-energy errors than TOR-TILD or similar EAM-reference approaches.
The reduction in path mismatch will persist across varying HEA compositions and temperatures.
The proposed method applies to near-equiatomic transition-metal and refractory HEAs.
A temperature range of approximately 1200–2000 K spans melting conditions for the HEAs within the proposed scope.
Successful application requires an ML training database with sufficiently dense sampling of liquid configurations.
The magnitude of improvement depends on training-set representativeness, ML-potential type, and alloy composition.
The decisive benchmark is a same-composition, same-temperature comparison of ML-reference and EAM-reference free-energy or path-integration discrepancies against ab initio calculations.
Failure of the ML reference to produce consistently smaller free-energy path mismatch than the EAM reference would falsify the hypothesis.
